# Understanding reactivity

Your task today is to improve two Shiny apps with *reactive expressions*.

## Part 1: a puzzling app (on your own)

Download [`24-reactivity.R`](https://stat220-f26.github.io/files/24-reactivity.R) (clicking the link downloads the file) and run the app.

1. What changes when you change...
    a. the number of bootstrap resamples?
    b. the number of histogram bins?
    c. the confidence level?
2. Change **only** the number of bins. Besides the bin width, does the shape of the histogram change? Does the table change? Then change **only** the confidence level. Does anything change that you didn't expect?

## Part 2: with those around you (groups of ~3)

3. Compare notes on Part 1.
4. Read the code in the `renderPlot()` and `renderTable()` expressions. What task do they both do?
5. Is anything replicated? What *should* update when the number of bins changes? What *shouldn't*?

::: callout-warning
## Stop here

Stop here and let Amanda know that you've finished. We'll regroup and discuss reactivity.
:::

## Part 3: fix the bootstrap app

6. Create a list of the values that should be calculated *once* and shared. Which inputs should each depend on?
7. Reorganize the server code. First create the reactive expression(s) with `reactive({ })`, **above** the `render` functions. Then edit `renderPlot()` and `renderTable()` to use them (remember the parentheses!). Run the app regularly.
8. Compare the revised app to the original. What changed when you move each slider? Do the plot and the table agree now?

# The manager survey app

Return to the app from Friday: your own version, or paste in [`v2-filter/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v2-filter/app.R) (**Copy raw file**, then paste over your `app.R`).

9. The `filter(industry %in% input$industry)` code is written twice. Create a reactive expression called `filtered()` and use it in both plots.
10. Add `req(input$industry)` as the first line of `filtered()`. Uncheck every industry. What changed?
11. Add a `textOutput("n_respondents")` that says "Showing 7,003 respondents", using `filtered()`. (Hint: `paste("Showing", scales::comma(nrow(filtered())), "respondents")`.)
12. Add a table of the filtered data: `DT::dataTableOutput("data")` in the UI and `DT::renderDataTable({ filtered() })` in the server.

The finished version is [`v3-reactive/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v3-reactive/app.R).

# UI design

## Warm up: what makes an app good?

Open the following shinyapps and explore a little bit.

+ [Data Wrangling](https://psu-eberly.shinyapps.io/data_wrangling/)
+ [Biodiversity in NPS](https://abenedetti.shinyapps.io/bioNPS/)
+ [Hex Memory Game](https://dreamrs.shinyapps.io/memory-hex/)
+ [Lake Profile Dashboard](https://gallery.shinyapps.io/lake-profile-dashboard/)

With the folks around you, discuss:

1. Did any apps stand out as enjoyable or useful?
2. What features or design choices make an app stand out?
3. Are there any small tweaks that would make them more usable?

## Reorganize the manager survey app

Start from your `v3` app, or [`v3-reactive/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v3-reactive/app.R). The finished version for today is [`v4-layout/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v4-layout/app.R) (try to build it yourself first!).

13. Move the inputs into a `sidebarPanel()` and the outputs into a `mainPanel()`, inside `sidebarLayout()`.
14. Put each plot, and the data table, on its own tab (`tabsetPanel()` and `tabPanel()`).
15. Give every input a plain-language label (not `xcol`!), and add axis labels and titles to the plots.
16. Add a fourth tab with a line plot of the *average* salary by `education`, with one line for each selected industry.

::: callout-tip
## Hint

`group_by(industry, education) |> summarize(mean_salary = mean(annual_salary))`, then `geom_line()` with `group = industry`. Don't forget to use `filtered()`!
:::

17. (If time) 25 checkboxes make the sidebar very long. Can you replace them with a `selectInput(..., multiple = TRUE)`?
